title: Sperm Chromatin Structure Assay (SCSA®) for Fertility Assessment
author: Evenson
materials: Purified water for reagents and FCM Sheath fluid

steps.title: Prepare AO staining buffer
steps.instruction: Combine 370 ml of 0.10 M citric acid buffer with 630 ml of 0.20 M Na₂PO₄ buffer, add 372 mg (1 mM) disodium EDTA (FW = 372.24) and 8.77 g NaCl (0.15 M); stir overnight on a stir plate until the EDTA is fully dissolved, adjust the pH to 6.0 with saturated NaOH solution, and store the buffer at 4 °C for up to several months.

steps.title: Prepare AO working solution
steps.instruction: Add 600 µl of AO stock solution (1 mg ml⁻¹) to each 100 ml of the prepared staining buffer, keep the mixture in a glass amber automatic dispenser, and store at 4 °C for 2–3 weeks.

steps.title: Set flow cytometer gains (Method 2)
steps.instruction: Using a reference sample, set the flow cytometer green (AO‑green, 515–530 nm BP) and red (AO‑red, 630 nm LP) fluorescent gains to the fixed positions: AO‑green at 475 ± 5/1024 and AO‑red at 125 ± 5/1024 on a linear 1024 × 1024 cytogram.

steps.title: Load AO‑stained semen and acquire data
steps.instruction: Place the AO‑stained semen sample into the flow cytometer; if using Method 1, adjust the green fluorescence so the main population is just short of halfway up the Y‑axis and the red fluorescence to about one‑fifth of the X‑axis on a linear 1024 × 1024 cytogram. For Method 2, the gains are already set as above.

steps.title: Create cytogram gates for analysis
steps.instruction: On the green‑versus‑red cytogram, establish four gates:

substeps.instruction: 1. Horizontal gate near the top to exclude diploid somatic epithelial cells and leukocytes.
2. Horizontal gate touching the top of the cigar‑shaped main sperm population; sperm above this line constitute the HDS fraction (excess histones).
3. Straight or curved gate on the right side of the normal sperm population.
4. 45‑degree angle gate touching the bottom of the main sperm population to exclude apoptotic/dead sperm and seminal debris.
5. Define the region between gates 3 and 4 as the %DFI (sperm with broken DNA).
6. Use the software to calculate %DFI and %HDS from the gated populations.

steps.title: Analyze data to calculate %DFI and %HDS
steps.instruction: Convert the green‑versus‑red cytogram to a Y = (green + red)/2 versus X = red/(red + green) plot (mean DFI scale 0–1 × 1000), generate a frequency histogram, set the cut‑off point separating sperm with and without broken DNA, and compute the percentages of %DFI and %HDS (and optionally other parameters such as moderate/high DFI, mean DFI, SD DFI).

steps.title: Send frozen semen aliquots for validation
steps.instruction: Freeze 15–20 semen aliquots that have been measured on the original Ortho flow cytometer, ship them to a new diagnostic center, and compare the %DFI results to ensure close correlation with the original measurements.
